Manage project memory
Claude regenerates project memory every evening from your past chats in this project. Only you can see this memory, and it is not shared with other project users.

Purpose & context

Kushal (GitHub: kusl) is building MyRestaurant — a self-hosted, single-restaurant ordering and management system licensed under AGPL-3.0. The stack is .NET 10 Blazor static SSR with interactive server islands, PostgreSQL 17, Dapper (EF Core explicitly forbidden), DbUp startup migrations, xUnit v3 with Testcontainers, Playwright for end-to-end tests, rootless Podman Compose, Caddy/Cloudflare tunnels, and OpenTelemetry. Dependency direction is strict: WebApplication → DataAccess → Domain (Domain is BCL-only). The repo lives at kusl/myrestaurant.

The project follows a rigorous spec-first, milestone/slice discipline. All behaviour changes, requirement edits, spec edits, ADR entries, and defect ledger rows must land atomically in the same slice. A living TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md (currently v1.45) tracks every decision, with a versioned changelog and a numbered findings ledger (F-series). BUILD_PROGRESS.md, MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md, DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md, and _CHANGES.md are updated in every slice.

M1–M5 are complete. M6 (hardening and menu enhancement) is the active milestone.

Current state

The most recently delivered slice is M6 Slice 60, which closed the last open item on the menu enhancement plan: allowing guests to like a dish that is currently unavailable. The mechanism adds a sibling .order-menu-inspect control beside disabled menu cards so guests can open the detail panel (and press the like button) without enabling the staging control. The specification is at v1.45. The predicted passing test count after Slice 60 is 1281; the §16.3 end-to-end suite stands at 21 scenarios.

Active context to carry forward:

Session-memory drift is a recurring hazard. The SHA-256 reconstruction ritual from dump.txt has caught drift four times, sometimes by five or more slices. Every session must begin with reconstruction and verification before any authoring.
Predicted test counts are arithmetic predictions, not observed results. Any deviation from the stated count is the first thing to investigate at the start of the next session.
Finding F-113 was discovered in Slice 60: ChosenItemDetail.Facts keyed a dictionary on <dt> inner text while CSS applies text-transform: uppercase, producing AVAILABLE where the record documented Available. This had been undetectable for nineteen slices because the dictionary had no caller.
On the horizon

The menu enhancement plan (tracked in MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md) has been completed as of Slice 60.
No explicit next slice has been named; the session ending on Slice 60 closed the last open menu item.
Previously deferred or noted gaps: no §16.3 scenario for /kitchen; no scenario for either resequencing verb; the wide layout stacking issue.
Context dump size management remains an ongoing concern (last measured reduction was ~14% in Slice 46; further reduction deferred).
Key learnings & principles

Delivery and workflow

Always deliver complete files in a structured .tar.gz archive with repo-relative paths, extractable at the repository root in one operation. Never deliver diffs, patches, or bespoke text-manipulation scripts.
Always explicitly list files to delete (even when the answer is none) and call out new files requiring git add (gates use git ls-files and miss untracked files).
Always update all documentation (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md, DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md, BUILD_PROGRESS.md, MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md, _CHANGES.md) in the same slice as code changes.
State the predicted test count arithmetically before packaging; explain every move. Any count moving without explanation is the first thing to investigate.
Gate discipline

The §16.4 counted-class census, Markdown table gate, version header gate, platform-state gate, Razor-directive gate, and byte hygiene checks (no CR, exactly one final newline, no trailing whitespace) must all be emulated against the working copy before packaging.
All gate assertions must be proven sensitive by planted defects before delivery — never vacuous (F-41).
Gates must key on CSS selectors (open parenthesis distinguishing a call from a mention) not bare identifiers, per F-67's principle.
The @section identifier is a reserved Razor word (RZ2005/RZ1011) — never use it as a variable name.
Architecture and code conventions

Append-only event tables with named vocabulary constraints and DISTINCT ON fold views.
New migrations must touch nothing existing.
Guid.CreateVersion7() is unordered within a millisecond; monotonicity is a stated contract of IIdentifierFactory.Create() (RFC 9562 §6.2 method 1 counter in rand_a).
Npgsql materializes timestamptz as UTC DateTime; Dapper constructor binding refuses DateTimeOffset — use an internal row type with DateTime fields and project to DateTimeOffset in a ToSummary() method.
string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, …): every operand in the chain must be a $"…" interpolated string — plain literals cause CS1620.
No await inside interpolated string holes (CS4007).
CSS text-transform is applied at render time; InnerTextAsync returns transformed text while TextContentAsync returns DOM text — use TextContentAsync plus whitespace collapsing for harness comparisons.
Delete unenforceable prose rather than correct it (F-77). Delete stale counts rather than update them (F-89 reversing F-73).
The data-loaded / data-live attribute pattern distinguishes interactive surface states for Playwright waits.
Testing

No Moq; hand-written fakes only. No FluentAssertions; use xUnit Assert or AwesomeAssertions.
Testcontainers integration tests skip when no container engine is present.
.slnx solution format only — never regenerate .sln.
New test classes require the TestingSectionContractTests counted-class floor to be updated in the same slice.
The §16.4 gate stops parsing number words at twelve; paragraphs covering more than one class must be split.
Finding management

Every finding gets a ledger row in DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md and Appendix A of the specification.
Findings are named something executable (F-38's pattern).
Decisions worth the person's potential veto are flagged explicitly with reversion instructions in _CHANGES.md.
Approach & patterns

Session start ritual: Reconstruct the full working tree from dump.txt via SHA-256 verification. Confirm slice number and verified test baseline before any authoring. Disclose any drift explicitly in BUILD_PROGRESS.md.
Slice scoping: Each slice is a discrete, verifiable unit. The "one change, one green run" principle applies unless the two changes produce distinguishable failure modes (documented reasoning required).
Veto pattern: Consequential design decisions are flagged as named veto candidates with explicit reversion instructions before packaging.
"What was NOT verified" discipline: Every BUILD_PROGRESS.md entry explicitly records what was not compiled, run, or browser-tested.
Byte hygiene: Every archived file is checked for CR characters, exactly one final newline, and no trailing whitespace before packaging.
CSS vocabulary: One breakpoint tree-wide (min-width: 48rem), handheld-first, shared .record-* / .page-head* / .manage-* vocabulary enforced by HandheldLayoutContractTests.
BUILD_PROGRESS.md: Too large to regenerate as a full file in most sessions — deliver as a targeted append or full file depending on session context. The docs/_append/ delivery mechanism is retired; ship the full file.
Communication style: terse and directive is the person's preference. Resume immediately on "please continue" or "continue" without preamble.
Tools & resources

Repository access: dump.txt (full repo export with SHA-256 per file); GitHub repo kusl/myrestaurant (main branch).
Stack: .NET 10, PostgreSQL 17, Dapper, DbUp, xUnit v3, Testcontainers, Playwright, rootless Podman Compose, Caddy, Cloudflare tunnels, OpenTelemetry.
Key documents: docs/TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md (v1.45), docs/MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md, docs/DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md, docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md, docs/OPERATIONS.md, docs/adr/.
Gate scripts: scripts/check_tree.sh, scripts/check_repository.sh, scripts/ci_local.sh; CI via .github/workflows/ci.yml and release.yml.
No .NET SDK in the authoring sandbox — all C# is written to spec and compiled by Kushal; Razor components are the most likely site of compiler-caught issues.
